newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares turn tail at mid session.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares turn tail at mid session.

text.p: Share prices on the Delhi Stock Exchange reversed early trends to drift lower in mid session trade on Thursday as investors booked profits at higher levels, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index was 1.91 points lower at 660.11 at 1:15 p.m. (0745 GMT). The index was 13.79 points higher at 675.81 in early trade.
Traders said a slowdown in buying by financial institutions also helped push share prices down.

"The market behaviour suggests that major players continued to adopt a cautious approach and preferred to book profits at every rise which mainly halted the rally in share prices," said Suresh Aggarwal of brokers Jaimata Securities.
Cement maker ACC dropped 8.05 rupees to 1,028 on heavy selling by speculators, brokers said.
Reliance Industries dropped three rupees to 191.40 on profit-taking.
State Bank of India slipped four rupees to 211.70.
Larsen and Toubro lost 4.70 rupees to 208.70.
